text.p: Salomon Brothers is maintaining its "hold" recommendation on Finnish steel group Rautaruukki Oy but is concerned about the stock's long-term value, Salomon said in a research note dated March 13.
"Although Rautaruukki's shares no longer trade at a premium and may rise with the sector, we are concerned about the stock's long-term value," Salomon Brothers said.
"In the long term we remain concerned that Rautaruukki will find it harder to add value than the market believes," Salomon Brothers said.
"The 1995 acquisition of (long steel products maker) Fundia may become a lasting burden," it said.

"Fundia's poorer than expected third-tertial 1996 earnings reflected the difficulties in achieving profitability in its commodity long products sectors, no matter how good the management and the resources," it said.
Fundia's higher-quality bar products business could also be "a liabiltity, as several producers ... have already discovered," it said.
"Rautaruukki's penetration of eastern European markets may not progress sufficiently quickly to justify investors' expectations," Salomon Brothers said.

The substantial expansion of capacity at Raahe over the next three years may mean that Rautaruukki's product mix could be diluted to fill capacity and that new capacity may hit the market during a cyclical downturn," it said.

"Rautaruukki's gearing has increased in the past 12 months to 129 percent. We believe a significant fall in the debt and interest burden is unlikely before 1998, except from the proceeds of an equity issue," it said.
Salomon Brothers added that Rautaruukki's gearing was "one of the highest levels in the European steel industry."

Despite those long-term concerns, Rautaruukki was no longer overvalued compared with other carbon steelmakers after underperforming the Finnish market by 20 percent since November, Salomon Brothers said.
"We are now more positive on the share, given the company's well-contained upstream costs, and the prospects of benefits from both capacity expansion and steel market recovery," it said.
Based on the current number of shares in issue, Salomon Brothers forecast 1997 earnings per share at 7.20 markka and 1998 EPS at 8.93 markka, up from 4.98 markka in 1996.
Salomon Brothers forecast Rautaruukki's 1997 p/e ratio at 6.6 and the 1998 p/e at 5.3.
